historical_reviews.related_cases: This is a passive RAS database/service health check, not an error-injection test. Existing records require attribution but must not be cleared to manufacture a clean result.

original_test_intent: Confirm the supported rasdaemon tooling can be installed/used, its data-collection service and database are operational, and `ras-mc-ctl --summary` reports no relevant RAS error counts for the defined observation window.
original_method: Record OS/kernel/platform and package state; obtain approval before package/service changes; preserve existing logs/database; capture service/database readiness and a baseline full `ras-mc-ctl --summary`; run the same full summary after the defined review window; compare every category/count and correlate any nonzero or increased count with timestamped kernel/AER/EDAC/MCE evidence without clearing records.
manual_activity: The OS/platform owner approves rasdaemon package installation or service enablement when absent and defines the observation window; the agent can collect the exact summary and correlated logs after approval.
required_inputs: Supported rasdaemon package/repository/version for the installed OS/kernel
Owner decision on install, enable or start actions if tooling/service is absent
Expected rasdaemon service unit and database/backend location/permissions
Observation window and policy for preexisting nonzero counts versus newly increased counts
Required RAS categories for this platform, including PCIe AER/EDAC/MCE coverage as applicable
Escalation policy for nonzero/increased counts and package/service rollback expectation
safety_requirements: Do not install packages, enable/start/restart services or modify repositories without approval
Do not clear rasdaemon database, dmesg, journal, AER or EDAC evidence
Capture full summary output; do not use `head`/`tail` to hide categories
Treat command exit0 separately from zero error counts and service/database freshness
If counts increase or severe events appear, preserve evidence and stop unrelated stress/fault tests; no automatic repair/retry
agent_execution_scope: Perform read-only package/version, service, database freshness and baseline summary checks
After approval, install/enable only the approved package/service and collect full source-command results
Do not clear evidence, inject errors, change kernel parameters, restart unrelated services, suppress historical records or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve package/repository and any service-state change
Define observation window and preexisting-count acceptance policy
Confirm platform-relevant categories and severity escalation
Review full summary/delta/log correlation and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Partial mismatch: `systemctl status` is a useful prerequisite, but `rasdaemon -r | tail` does not replace the source `ras-mc-ctl --summary` and truncation can omit error categories.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use full `ras-mc-ctl --summary` as the primary source-aligned command before and after the defined window; supplement with untruncated service/package/database status and timestamped kernel/AER/EDAC/MCE logs. Do not clear evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: rasdaemon installation, OS execution, exact `ras-mc-ctl --summary`, no-error intent, Common branch and 15/15-minute scope are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Validate package/service/database readiness and compare full source-aligned summary category counts across a defined window with log correlation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds provenance, database freshness, baseline-delta semantics and complete evidence while retaining the literal source command instead of the historical substitution.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An active service or `rasdaemon -r` output does not by itself satisfy `ras-mc-ctl --summary`; exit status alone also does not prove zero error counts or fresh collection.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Summary counts may be cumulative and historical; passive observation cannot prove error-detection paths work under injected faults.

project_override_considerations: No project-specific hardware override is needed. Preserve historical RAS evidence and interpret counts using platform/kernel/package provenance rather than a generic zero-output assumption.
expected_evidence: OS/kernel/platform identity and rasdaemon package/version/repository status
Service unit state, start time, database/backend path, permissions and freshness
Full untruncated baseline and post-window `ras-mc-ctl --summary` outputs with exit codes/timestamps
Per-category before/after count matrix and explicit zero/nonzero/delta interpretation
Correlated dmesg/journal/PCIe AER/EDAC/MCE records for any counts
Approved install/service-change transcript if applicable, final service state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source purpose, exact command and no-error acceptance are coherent. It needs stronger cumulative-count/time-window interpretation, but no source field contradicts the intended passive RAS check.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Package/service prerequisites and observation policy are identifiable. Their absence is a normal RPUC gate, not a semantic or safety blocker.

review_improvement: Restores the literal `ras-mc-ctl --summary`, eliminates output truncation, separates service readiness from error counts and adds full baseline-delta/log correlation without clearing evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: The source explicitly names `ras-mc-ctl --summary`, which reports database-backed category counts. Replacing it with service status plus another rasdaemon mode changes coverage: a daemon may be active while its database is stale, inaccessible or contains nonzero counts. Conversely, a historical count is not automatically a new test-window failure. The correct static contract therefore preserves full summaries at two timestamps, validates database freshness and reports both absolute counts and deltas for engineer adjudication.
